transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-04-21 14:00 UTC
- Duration: 54 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Ortiz (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Noah Li (Redwood CSM); Ravi Patel (Head of ML, Ebblight), Lina Gomez (VP Eng), Owen Price (Infra), Sana Iqbal (Security)

Auto-generated summary (may be incomplete):
Quick renewal + expansion check-in. Customer is evaluating a move to a Dedicated reserved pool for predictable latency during their Q3 launch, and wants an additional EU region + VPC/KMS details. Discussed latency/cost tradeoffs, batching and KV cache behavior with their named NER workload, and next steps include micro-benchmarks, pricing worksheet, and a security deep-dive.

Topics covered:
- Current usage and spike patterns
- Dedicated vs hosted fallback strategy
- EU region onboarding timeline and data residency concerns
- Security: KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML, SOC 2 references
- Action items and next steps

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Ortiz: ok hi everyone, thanks for joining. we got about 50 minutes, we'll run through status, talk capacity and the region ask. Ravi, Lina, you good to start?
[00:08] Ravi Patel: yeah thanks Maya. yep good here. thanks.
[00:11] Lina Gomez: hi all. just quick note—we have a hard launch window in early Q3 so this is kind of time sensitive for provisioning.
[00:20] Maya Ortiz: great, that's helpful. Noah, are you on the timeline?
[00:23] Noah Li: yep noted. we flagged Q3 in the renewal playbook. we'll prioritize.
[00:27] Devon Park: hi, Devon here. i'd like to focus the technical piece on latency SLOs for their NER inference and cost curve if we move to Dedicated.

[00:34] Lina Gomez: we're seeing a tail latency issue on long documents—so 3k token-ish docs occasionally. average token length's around 1k but there's a heavy tail.
[00:44] Devon Park: understood. that tail drives KV cache pressure and also increases per-token compute. have you profiled sequence-length distribution?
[00:50] Ravi Patel: yeah we have histograms, can share. the 95th hits about 3.2k.
[00:55] Devon Park: ok that's useful. two quick notes—Redwood Dedicated gives you pinned GPU pools which improves jitter, and we can pin model variants optimized for long context. but there's a cost delta vs hosted.
[01:10] Lina Gomez: what magnitude are we talking about—ballpark cost uplift?
[01:12] Maya Ortiz: depends on commit size. i'll send the updated commitment worksheet after the call. rough rule: predictable dedicated SLOs start to make sense at steady token volumes north of ~12–15M tokens / month, otherwise the hosted + smart routing + KV caching sometimes is cheaper.
[01:28] Owen Price: our forecasts show a steady ramp; we think we'll be ~18M tokens/month at launch. question—can Dedicated autoscale for bursts?
[01:36] Devon Park: yes, we offer configurable burst capacity. the Dedicated pool can have reserved baseline and a burst policy to consume extra capacity; falls back to hosted model variants if reserves depleted.
[01:46] Ravi Patel: how's the fallback handled? we can't have unpredictable model changes in prod.
[01:52] Devon Park: good question. its policy-driven: you define allowed model families for fallback; we can keep same model family but a lower quantization or a slightly smaller architecture. and the router annotates responses so you know when a fallback happened.
[02:05] Lina Gomez: annotated responses are critical. can we get traceability in logs and correlation ids?
[02:12] Noah Li: yes, per-request trace ids map to route and model metadata, available in the Console and audit logs.

[02:18] Sana Iqbal: on security—KMS integration is a showstopper for us. we need bring-your-own-key and HSM-backed encryption, and audit logs for all model calls.
[02:27] Maya Ortiz: we support customer-managed keys (KMS) and HSM workflows in our Private and Dedicated offerings. i will share the KMS integration doc.
[02:34] Sana Iqbal: also SOC 2 type II evidence and our legal team will want retention windows for logs.
[02:40] Maya Ortiz: we can provide SOC 2 artifacts and explain log retention options. there's an add-on for extended retention.

[02:46] Owen Price: EU region onboarding—what's the lead time for stand-up in eu-west-1?
[02:52] Devon Park: typical provisioning for a new geocluster is 6–8 weeks if it's Dedicated with VPC peering and customer network config; onboarding to Hosted EU is faster—about 2 weeks. the longer path is private on-prem stacks which need packaging and air-gap validation.
[03:08] Lina Gomez: 6–8 weeks is tight but workable. we need to know cutover steps because we can't have data crossing borders during the transition window.
[03:16] Devon Park: absolutely. we can orchestrate a staged cutover with routing policies—initial read-only traffic, then canary writes, and finally full cutover. all in Console with rollout controls.

[03:28] Ravi Patel: benchmarking—we need a real micro-benchmark on our NER model to validate latency and token cost after quantization.
[03:33] Devon Park: we can run the benchmark if you share a representative prompt set and model weights (or we can pull a workspace sample). i'll run it on Dedicated-like instance types, with batching configs that match your QPS.
[03:45] Ravi Patel: ok we'll share a 200-sample set.
[03:48] Devon Park: perfect. i'll include comparisons: hosted baseline, dedicated baseline, and a quantized fp16/INT8 variant.

[03:54] Lina Gomez: how does prefix caching behave for repeated queries—our users often send similar bios and clinical notes; will kv cache reduce token cost?
[04:02] Devon Park: yes, prefix/KV cache helps a lot for overlapping contexts—we see 20–60% token reduction on certain workloads. caveat: cache hit rate depends on prompt normalization.
[04:12] Ravi Patel: any compatibility issues with long-context models and cache?
[04:16] Devon Park: only edge cases; cache gets invalidated on model version changes unless you pin model versions. good practice is pinning for canaries.

[04:25] Lina Gomez: procurement timeline—our procurement needs a clear committed spend and SLA. can you provide a two-option quote: (1) 12-month Dedicated commit with burst; (2) 6-month Hosted+Dedicated hybrid?
[04:36] Maya Ortiz: yes we'll provide both. I'll draft two SKUs and call out the unit economics and SLA differences.

[04:44] Owen Price: one more infra question—VPC peering and egress. we need to know bandwidth costs and NAT requirements.
[04:51] Devon Park: we'll put the VPC diagram and egress estimation in the network appendix. for egress, we break down by region and the Console shows egress est per token.

[04:58] Sana Iqbal: is there a way to get a proof-of-environment for KMS encryption—like KMS attestation?
[05:05] Maya Ortiz: yes we can include attestation docs and a security contact to walk through the KMS handshake.

[05:11] Ravi Patel: on the competitor front—we evaluated LambdaScale, their cost looked lower but they had weaker multi-region support and less mature observability. any differences on observability?
[05:22] Noah Li: Redwood Console gives per-route token-level cost, latency percentiles, and model regression alerts tied to prompt sets; those eval hooks are one of our differentiators.

[05:30] Lina Gomez: will you share the card with per-route cost drilldowns so we can map to our cost centers?
[05:35] Maya Ortiz: yes we'll share a sample CSV and a Console view screenshot.

[05:40] Ravi Patel: ok recap—we want Dedicated baseline with burst, EU region provisioning, KMS BYOK, SOC 2 artifacts, and benchmark on our NER.
[05:48] Maya Ortiz: yep. to be explicit:
[05:50] - we'll send a dual-SKU quote and the dedicated commitment worksheet (Maya)
[05:53] - Devon runs micro-benchmarks on the sample prompts and returns a spreadsheet with latency/cost comparisons
[05:58] - Noah will prepare the Console screenshots and sample CSVs for cost mapping
[06:02] - Sana will send compliance questions; we'll set a security deep-dive follow-up (Noah + Security).

[06:08] Lina Gomez: sounds good. timeframe on the docs?
[06:11] Maya Ortiz: i'll get the pricing worksheet by Friday (2026-04-23). Devon's benchmark by next Tues (2026-04-28). security deep-dive week of 2026-04-27.

[06:20] Ravi Patel: small nit—if we commit, can we lock latency SLOs for the 95th percentile? need to know what SLA math looks like and remedies.
[06:29] Devon Park: standard is 95th percentile latency SLOs in Dedicated contracts; remedies are credits and guaranteed remediation plan. we'll put the SLA appendix in the quote.
[06:38] Owen Price: last point—does Dedicated support hot model swapping during rollouts? we want zero-downtime canaries.
[06:44] Devon Park: yes, we support canary rollouts with traffic-splitting and automatic rollback on regressions. Console traces rollouts and error budgets.

[06:52] Lina Gomez: ok appreciate it. anything else on billing—do you offer monthly invoicing or only quarterly?
[06:58] Maya Ortiz: standard offerings include monthly invoicing for committed customers, and we can discuss enterprise billing terms if needed.

[07:05] Ravi Patel: great. thanks all.
[07:08] Maya Ortiz: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the artifacts.

[07:12] (end of recording)
